## Historical audit — S0224

**Scope:** Chunk 1 of 3 only. All citations refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_1/results/r1/scene_rsi_v2_1/C2/test/commons_189918915/trajectory.jsonl`. Neither the reference nor the rendered image is visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 1 | The goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate editable meshes and matching viewpoint, materials and occlusions. The student’s inventory interpreted it as a warehouse with racks, pallet loads, roof, skylight and fixtures; that interpretation is not independently verified (student `model_response`, line 3). |
| Student `model_response`, line 3; `execute`, line 4 | The first complete program constructed multiple named assets and child boxes: two racks, 32 pallet loads, roof, skylight, lights and wall. Pallet slats, runners and cargo were grouped in load assets and positioned relative to shelves; physical contact or correct connections were not independently checked. |
| Student `model_response`, line 3 | The program specified colors, procedural noise/bump, emission, area lights, an upward-looking camera with roll, exposure and glow. These are implemented settings, not proof of matching texture, pose, illumination or framing. |
| `execution_result`, line 5, characters [0,165586); `select`, line 6 | Step 1 reported `ok: true`, completed rendering, saved `final.png` and `scene.blend`, and was selected. This is **formal execution success**, not visual or geometric correctness. |
| Student `model_request`, line 7, characters [0,189997); `codex_session`, line 8 | The next request supplied the reference and first render for comparison. Both student sessions reported zero tool calls; the visible autonomous exploration consists of the build and subsequent review, not separate tool-based investigation. |
| Student `model_response`, line 9 | The student reported pale cargo/framework, insufficient dark shelf gaps, oversized end wall and too much opposite rack. Its revised program restored material base colors, narrowed loads, extended the aisle, moved the opposite rack, changed camera aim/roll and adjusted lighting. These are student diagnoses and proposed code changes; their correctness and execution are not visible in this chunk. |

**Teacher input and adoption:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update appears in the visible observations. The comparison instruction and render were runner feedback, not teacher advice. There is therefore no visible evidence of teacher receipt or adoption.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** The first build succeeded technically; overall reconstruction quality and final outcome are **unknown**. The revision is nonempty, but this chunk ends at its response: no second execution, validation, final selection or interruption is shown. In particular, apparent material color, multiple-object coverage, rack/load contact, camera pose, and light or rendering defects cannot be verified without the images. The student’s color-node explanation is a hypothesis, not an established cause.

**Lessons:** Transferably, a successful render establishes executability rather than image fidelity, and a review can distinguish local geometry from camera/material hypotheses. Task-specific choices—warehouse inventory, shelf spacing and camera adjustments—remain unverified; unseen chunks cannot resolve them here.
